papers.title: Cyclic homology of Sheaf Categories
papers.abstract: In this note, we explain the circle action on the Hochschild homology of categories of sheaves and their admissible subcategories in terms of the six-functor formalism using factorization homology, including (quasi-)coherent sheaves on derived stacks, sheaves on manifolds with prescribed microsupports, and Tamarkin categories with prescribed microsupports. We also explain the Gysin sequence for $C_\ell$ and $S^1$-(co)invariants and the K\"unneth sequence for $S^1$-(co)invariants of the Hochschild homology relative to any complex-oriented symmetric monoidal category.

papers.title: Ice and mirrors
papers.abstract: Given a mirror pair of smooth affine principal upper cluster varieties admitting reddening sequences, we show that homological mirror symmetry for principal cluster varieties -- assumed compatible with certain cluster structures -- descends under freezing. This allows us to induct on the following class. A skew-symmetrizable matrix is peelable if, by mutations and removing sinks or sources, it can be reduced to the empty matrix; it is sub-peelable if it is a principal submatrix of a peelable matrix. We establish homological mirror symmetry for full rank upper cluster varieties whose mutable matrix is sub-peelable. We show sub-peelability for the Fock--Goncharov SL(n) quiver for any compact surface with nonempty boundary, all of whose boundaries have markings. Consequently, we establish homological mirror symmetry between the moduli of decorated SL(n) local systems and the corresponding pinned PGL(n) spaces. The results were obtained using ChatGPT Astra.

papers.title: Deformation Quantization of Coisotropic A-branes
papers.abstract: Motivated by the Gukov--Witten proposal that the endomorphism algebra of a coisotropic A-brane should be described by a deformation quantization of its transverse holomorphic symplectic geometry at the perturbative level, we study deformation quantization on transverse holomorphic symplectic manifolds $(M,\Omega)$. Extending the approach of Nest--Tsygan to this setting, we show that, under an admissibility condition, equivalence classes of deformation quantizations are in bijection with \[ \hbar H^2\bigl(\operatorname{F}_1\Omega^\bullet(M,\mathbb C),d\bigr) [[\hbar]], \] where $\operatorname{F}_1\Omega^\bullet(M,\mathbb C)$ is the differential ideal generated by transverse $(1,0)$-forms. We further illustrate this framework through examples arising from mapping tori, $T$-duality, and coisotropic lifts in cotangent bundles. These examples clarify the roles of admissibility and the transverse Atiyah class, as well as the distinction between deformation quantizations and global star products. Finally, for a coisotropic A-brane $M$ induced from a transverse complex manifold $Q$, we use transverse jets and the Fock representation to construct a perturbative level action $End(M)\curvearrowright Hom(M,Q)$ under suitable compatibility assumptions, providing a geometric realization of the brane quantization philosophy.

papers.title: Torsion phenomena in symplectic capacities via Clarke duality
papers.abstract: We study Gutt--Hutchings capacities with finite cyclic coefficients and show that torsion in positive $S^1$-equivariant symplectic homology detects new obstructions to symplectic embeddings between convex toric domains. Prime-field coefficients give no additional obstructions in this class, while the torsion responsible for the new obstructions already appears over $\mathbb Z/p^{p+2}$ for every prime $p$. We prove a stabilization theorem for these capacities on convex bodies with arbitrary commutative coefficients, yielding a sharp stabilized embedding obstruction in an explicit example. Clarke duality makes these phenomena accessible to computation. We extend the filtered equivariant Clarke--Floer comparison to arbitrary commutative coefficient rings and compute the capacities using models of dual action sublevels built from representation spheres. The circle-action weights encode orbit covering multiplicities, whose products govern the new obstructions.

papers.title: Capacities from the Chiu-Tamarkin complex II: Product formula and toric domains
papers.abstract: In this article, we continue our study of equivariant symplectic capacities of open sets in a cotangent bundle defined via the Chiu-Tamarkin complex constructed from the microlocal theory of sheaves. The paper consists of two parts: 1) We develop the theory of $S^1$-equivariant Chiu-Tamarkin complex over complex-oriented ring spectra. 2) Applications of the theory to symplectic capacities: We show that a product formula for the capacities, whose Ekeland-Hofer capacities version is folklore since 1988, is not true via an (uncountable family of) counterexample(s). The counterexample (family) is the product of a concave toric domain of dimension $6$ ($2n\geq 6$) and a $2$-dimensional disk. We also prove a Weyl law of the capacities for all toric domains in dimension $2n$. The algebraic verification is based on a chain model for the Chiu-Tamarkin complex of all toric domains in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, which recovers Irie's conjectural chain model of $S^1$-equivariant symplectic homology for star-shaped toric domains (defined only) in $\mathbb{R}^4$.

papers.title: Derived sheaves in locally conformally symplectic geometry
papers.abstract: In this paper, we use derived sheaves to study rigidity phenomena in the cotangent bundles of manifolds endowed with some locally conformally symplectic ($\frak{lcs}$) structure. Taking inspiration from the work of Guillermou, Kashiwara and Shapira, we define a quantization for ``$\frak{lcs}$'' Hamiltonian isotopies, as well as new quantities: the asymptotic Betti numbers of a sheaf. We then show that those quantities are ``well behaved'' with respect of said quantization and use this to give a sheaf-theoretical proof of the Chantraine-Murphy theorem. We also consider the quantization in light of the Tamarkin morphism and the displacement energy of sheaves. This allows us to derive a non-squeezing theorem for $\frak{lcs}$ geometry that is similar, although not identical, to the one recently proven by Bertelson, Chakravarthy, and Sandon. Indeed, the result shown in this paper is more in line with the contact non-squeezing theorem shown by Eliashberg, Kim and Polterovich in 2006.

papers.title: Categorical structures of Kuranishi spaces with $L_{\infty}[1]$-algebras
papers.abstract: We introduce $L_{\infty}$-Kuranishi spaces by associating, to each chart, $L_{\infty}[1]$-algebras defined on open neighborhoods of points in the zero locus of the Kuranishi section. We show that these objects collectively form a category into which the category of smooth manifolds naturally embeds. Some notions in \cite{FOOO1} are modified to achieve the desired categorical structures; for instance, the tangent bundle condition for chart embeddings is replaced by a quasi-isomorphism condition for the $L_{\infty}[1]$-structures.

papers.title: Symplectic capacities and Weyl laws from Abelian Higgs min max theory
papers.abstract: For a Hermitian line bundle $E\to Y$ over a Riemannian manifold $(Y^n,g)$, the self-dual Abelian-Higgs energy is defined by $\mathcal{E}^Y_{\varepsilon,g}(u,a)=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_Y \left(|\nabla_a u|_g^2+\varepsilon^2|F_a|_g^2+ \frac{(1-|u|^2)^2}{4\varepsilon^2}\right)dV_g$, where $u$ is a smooth section of $E$, $a$ is a unitary connection, and $F_a$ is its curvature. Pigati and Stern studied the energy as a codimension-two analogue of the Allen-Cahn energy to study minimal submanifolds in a Riemannian manifold. In this paper, we use this functional to define a nondecreasing sequence of symplectic capacities $\{c_k^{\mathrm{AH}}\}_{k\ge1}$ in dimension four by a min-max construction. In particular, we prove that $c_1^{\mathrm{AH}}$ is normalized on the ball and the cylinder. For the upper bound on the cylinder, we combine Gromov's theory of families of $J$-holomorphic spheres with Taubes's planar vortex. For the lower bound on the ball, we use the properties of the Abelian-Higgs theory developed by Pigati-Stern, together with a geometric estimate on smooth approximations to the double of the ball and an equivariant deformation of low energy sublevels. These estimates give the normalization without Seiberg-Witten theory. We then use Seiberg-Witten moduli spaces on $\mathbb{CP}^2$ and $S^2\times S^2$ to prove an upper bound on the higher capacities of balls and the formula $c_k^{\mathrm{AH}}(Z^4(a),\omega_0)=ka$. We also prove Weyl laws for domains in $\mathbb{R}^4$, both for the capacity sequence and for the min-max sequence with the standard Euclidean metric. For these results, we construct AH sweepouts from moduli spaces of the solutions to the perturbed Seiberg-Witten equations.

papers.title: Legendrian surgery on the unit cotangent bundle of the Klein bottle and infinitely many Stein fillings
papers.abstract: We show that a single Legendrian surgery on the canonical contact structure of the unit cotangent bundle $ST^*K$ of the Klein bottle $K$ produces a planar contact $3$--manifold $(Y,\xi)$ with infinitely many pairwise non-homeomorphic Stein fillings. The fillings are obtained from the disk cotangent bundle $DT^*K$ by attaching a single Weinstein $2$--handle along the images of one Legendrian knot under the powers of a contactomorphism of $(ST^*K,\xi_{\mathrm{can}})$, no positive power of which extends over $DT^*K$. The construction takes place in a planar open book of $(ST^*K,\xi_{\mathrm{can}})$, and $(Y,\xi)$ is contactomorphic to Baykur's recent example of a planar contact $3$--manifold with infinitely many Stein fillings. Since $(ST^*K,\xi_{\mathrm{can}})$ has a unique minimal symplectic filling up to homeomorphism, finiteness of fillings is not preserved under Legendrian surgery, even for planar contact $3$--manifolds. The same construction gives the planar contact $3$--manifolds with infinitely many rational homology ball Stein fillings found earlier by the author.

papers.title: Deformation quantization of symplectic vector fields
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study deformation quantization of symplectic vector fields \`a la Fedosov. We provide an explicit construction to quantize each symplectic vector field as a derivation of the deformed star algebra. This recovers a result of M\"uller-Bahns and Neumaier with an explicit formula of higher total degree terms. Moreover, we show that this quantization yields a non-abelian $2$-cocycle on the Lie algebra of symplectic vector fields with values in the deformed star algebra. For a Fedosov deformation quantization with vanishing first characteristic class, this non-abelian $2$-cocycle can provide a formal deformation of the crossed-product algebra generated by the action of symplectic vector fields. In this sense, we can quantize any Lie algebra action by symplectic vector fields.

papers.title: Belavin--Drinfeld bivectors and Poisson deformations
papers.abstract: We study Belavin--Drinfeld Poisson bivectors $\pi_{(\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^r,\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^c)}$ on $\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times m}(\mathbb{C})$ from the perspective of Poisson deformation theory. We prove that the log-canonical part $\pi_0$ of $\pi_{(\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^r,\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^c)}$ is $\mathbb{T}_{(\mathbf{\Gamma}^r,\mathbf{\Gamma}^c)}$-log-symplectic if and only if the pair $(\mathbf{\Gamma}^r,\mathbf{\Gamma}^c)$ of Belavin--Drinfeld triples is aperiodic. In this case, we show that $\pi_{(\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^r,\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^c)}$ is a maximal $\mathbb{T}_{(\mathbf{\Gamma}^r,\mathbf{\Gamma}^c)}$-invariant Poisson deformation of $\pi_0$, and we construct a $\mathbb{T}_{(\mathbf{\Gamma}^r,\mathbf{\Gamma}^c)}$-equivariant Poisson birational map between $(\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times m},\pi_0)$ and $(\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times m},\pi_{(\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^r,\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^c)})$.

papers.title: Inference of Hamiltonian and Lie-Poisson structures from vector field samples
papers.abstract: We present a method for the data-driven inference of Hamiltonian and Lie-Poisson dynamical systems from vector-field samples, in which the Hamiltonian and the underlying Poisson tensor are estimated jointly rather than assuming the structure is known. The Hamiltonian is represented as a linear combination of random feature maps with fixed random internal weights, so its estimation is a linear regression problem for any given Poisson structure. We treat three cases of increasing generality: a known Poisson tensor, an unknown constant invertible (symplectic) structure matrix, and Lie-Poisson and affine Poisson structures, with structure matrix linear in the state. In the constant case, the Hamiltonian and structure matrix are recovered jointly from an eigenvalue problem that avoids the trivial zero solution due to the scaling symmetry of Hamiltonian systems. For Lie-Poisson and affine Poisson systems we alternate between an initial Hamiltonian estimate from a generalized eigenvalue problem for an approximate first integral, and a constrained nonlinear least-squares fit of the structure constants that enforces the Jacobi identity and, for affine structures, the cocycle condition, via continuation in a penalty parameter. Orthogonal matching pursuit selects a compact, well-conditioned subset of random features. Because the learned Hamiltonian is a sum of single-feature terms, the model admits an explicit Poisson/symplectic splitting integrator, which we use to validate the learned systems via long-time Poincare sections. We demonstrate the approach on the four- and five-dimensional Lorenz-86 model and a six-dimensional Kirchhoff rigid-body system, recovering Hamiltonians, structure constants and Casimir invariants to high accuracy, and showing the inferred Poincare sections converge to the correct invariant-tori topology as the number of random features increases.

papers.title: Length Spectrum Rigidity and Flexibility of Spheres of Revolution with One Equator
papers.abstract: We define a notion of marked length spectrum for $S^1$-symmetric Riemannian metrics on the two-sphere having only one equator. We prove that isospectral metrics in this class have conjugate geodesic flows. Under a further ${\mathbb Z}_2$-symmetry assumption, we show that the marked length spectrum determines the metric. Finally, we show that every isospectral class of metrics contains a unique ${\mathbb Z}_2$-symmetric metric and give an explicit description of this isospectral class as an infinite-dimensional convex set, generalizing the known description of $S^1$-symmetric Zoll metrics. This paper contains also two appendices, in which we provide an elementary proof of the fact that a $C^2$ real-valued function on an interval is determined by the set of tangent lines to its graph, and we classify a class of $S^1$-invariant contact forms on three-manifolds.
